audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with the packet in three rows and, as the packet defect says, hands Gnar five stages against a 59.02% Swain win rate with no row where Swain ever wins.
audit.why: Level 1 is Gnar's by the page's own whys[0] (Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against your 750 Q). Level 6 is his: full Rage plus GNAR! beats a 120-second ultimate you cannot hold. The 2+ item row is where the win rate actually comes from, and the mirror already flipped that row to Swain.
audit.corrected: win[0]/phases[0].side to Gnar, win[4]/phases[4].side to Gnar, win[6]/phases[6].side to Swain, with phases[6].why rewritten to match.

audit.why: Spike shape is right: he owns 1-2, he owns 6, his first item is a real threat, and your 2+ item window is the payoff. Wording inside spikes[1] needed the mechanical fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places say GNAR! cancels or interrupts Demonic Ascension, and spikes[1] calls GNAR! a 'point-and-click AOE stun wall-slam'. whys[2] also has Mega wall-slamming you at level 3.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a transform, not a channel — Riot's text says the form lasts indefinitely as long as he drains champions, and the kit carries no channel flag. The mirror reached the same conclusion. GNAR! is a directional throw that damages and slows; the stun only happens to enemies hurled into a wall. And at level 3 the wall-slam is not available at all — Mega's stun there is Wallop.
audit.corrected: GNAR! reframed as a displacement out of the 650 drain range rather than an interrupt, with the wall condition stated; level 3 threat corrected to Mega Wallop.

audit.why: The 'never press R into full Rage' rule is right, and it survives the correction above — the reason changes from 'he cancels it' to 'he removes you from it', but the behaviour is the same.
GNAR! at 90/60/30 seconds is not a cooldown you outwait in lane — Rage is the real timer, and the page already tracks Rage rather than a cooldown. That is the correct read.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Gnar carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on and your pattern peaks: Liandry's burn plus drain beats what Gnar trades back in a fight he cannot kite out of.

edits.before: Even with full kit your W-into-E combo is countered by his hop escape, and Mega-Gnar at level 3 can wall-slam you before your R is available to sustain it.
edits.after: Even with full kit your W-into-E is answered by Hop, and if he transforms at 3 his Mega Wallop stuns you flat — the wall-slam needs GNAR!, but that stun does not.

edits.before: GNAR! at level 6 hard-counters Demonic Ascension: he holds full Rage and explodes the moment you drain, stunning you into the wall and ending the healing window you needed.
edits.after: GNAR! answers Demonic Ascension by moving you, not by cutting it — the form has no channel, but thrown out of your 650 drain range, and into a wall for the stun, the healing simply stops.

edits.before: GNAR! gives him a point-and-click AOE stun wall-slam — if he catches you at low Rage he can hold it and explode when you press R, cancelling your drain window.
edits.after: GNAR! throws everything around him one direction and stuns only what lands on a wall — held for your R, it does not cancel the form, it hurls you out of the 650 drain range.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 belong to Gnar's GNAR! threat. In Mini form he out-pokes you; in Mega form he can wall-slam you and chain CC into a kill. The critical rule is never press R into a Gnar who has full or near-full Rage — he will walk up, take your drain for one second, then GNAR! stun you into the wall and you lose the exchange that was supposed to be your sustain window. Instead, bait him to spend Rage on a bad engage or wait for his Rage bar to reset after a missed Mega transform, then force a trade. Your W slow is your best tool: land it on Mini-Gnar as he repositions, then root the approach. Collect every fragment you can and do not die; the matchup flips entirely at your second item.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 belong to Gnar's Rage bar. In Mini form he out-pokes you; in Mega form Wallop stuns and GNAR! throws you into terrain. The critical rule is never press R into a Gnar at full or near-full Rage — he will walk up, eat one second of drain, then hurl you out of the 650 range you were healing inside. Nothing was interrupted; you were simply removed from your own ultimate, with a wall stun on top if he aims it. Instead, bait Rage onto a bad engage or wait out the reset after a missed transform, then force the trade. Vision of Empire is your best tool: slow him as he repositions, then throw E past him so the return pass roots the approach. Bank fragments and do not die; this flips at your second item.

edits.before: Build Rage to GNAR! the moment you press Demonic Ascension so your drain is immediately cancelled by the AOE stun
edits.after: Build Rage and GNAR! the moment you press Demonic Ascension, throwing you clear of drain range so the healing just stops

notes: The page told the player four times that GNAR! cancels Demonic Ascension. It does not — Riot's text says the form is indefinite while he drains champions and there is no channel flag, so the old advice quietly implied the drain was safe if you could avoid the 'interrupt'. The real mechanic is displacement out of the 650 drain radius, plus a stun only if you hit a wall, and the practical rule (never ult into full Rage) is unchanged. Also corrected GNAR! being called point-and-click, and a level-3 wall-slam that cannot exist — that stun is Mega Wallop. Chart rows 1, 5 and 7 flipped in matched pairs; the packet defect explicitly flagged a chart giving Gnar five stages against a 59.02% Swain win rate, and the 2+ item row is where that win rate lives.
